fields.title: Raw kingfish, verjus, salted raspberry
fields.intro: Nothing is cooked. The bottle supplies the acid, so the fish only needs salt, fat and something sharp on top.
steps: Slice the kingfish across the grain, 3mm, and lay it flat on a cold plate. Salt it lightly ten minutes before serving.
Crush a small handful of raspberries with a pinch of salt and a splash of NON1 straight from the bottle. Leave it to sit.
Spoon good olive oil over the fish, then the raspberry mixture, then a little more salt.
Finish with dill and a grind of pepper. Pour the NON1 cold, 6°C.
fields.why: The dish has no acid of its own — the verjus in NON1 becomes the dressing. Salt on both sides of the pairing means neither has to shout, and the chamomile tannin gives the fat somewhere to go.

fields.title: Whole roast fish, fennel, burnt lemon
fields.intro: One tray, one heat, no turning. The fennel goes sweet, the lemon goes bitter and the bottle sits between them.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Slice two fennel bulbs thin and toss with oil and plenty of salt in a large tray.
Halve a lemon and put it cut-side down in the tray. Roast fennel and lemon alone for 15 minutes.
Score the fish twice each side, salt it inside and out, and lay it on the fennel. Roast 20–25 minutes until the fin pulls free.
Squeeze the burnt lemon over everything at the table. Serve the NON1 very cold in a wine glass.
fields.why: Burnt lemon and roast fennel are both bitter-sweet, which is exactly where the salted raspberry sits. The bead in NON1 lifts the oil off your palate between mouthfuls.

fields.title: Oysters three ways, chamomile mignonette
fields.intro: A dozen and a half oysters, three dressings, one bottle. The mignonette is made with the wine you are drinking.
steps: Shuck 18 oysters, keep them on ice, and reserve the liquor.
Mignonette one: 60ml NON1, finely diced shallot, cracked pepper, a pinch of salt. Steep 20 minutes.
Mignonette two: crushed raspberry, verjus, chamomile tea reduced to a syrup. Cool it fully.
Mignonette three: nothing but a squeeze of lemon and Murray River salt — the control.
Serve six of each on rock salt. Pour the NON1 at 6°C and taste the plain ones first.
fields.why: Using NON1 in the mignonette puts the same salt-and-acid signature on the plate and in the glass. The plain oyster proves the point: the bottle is doing what a Chablis would.

fields.title: Miso mushrooms on toast, orange zest
fields.intro: Caramelised on caramelised. The mushrooms go dark, the miso goes sticky and the bottle meets both.
steps: Tear 300g of mixed mushrooms by hand. Get a dry pan very hot and add them with no oil — let them release and colour, 6 minutes.
Add a knob of butter, a tablespoon of white miso and a splash of water. Stir until it glazes.
Toast thick sourdough, rub it with garlic, pile the mushrooms on.
Grate orange zest over the top and crack pepper. Serve NON3 chilled, not iced.
fields.why: NON3 is built on 48-hour dehydrated orange, so the zest on the plate is a direct echo. Cinnamon tannin cuts the butter and stops the miso reading as sweet.

fields.title: Roast chicken, orange, cinnamon, bitter greens
fields.intro: The bottle in dish form: caramelised citrus, warm spice, something bitter to finish.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Dry the chicken thoroughly and salt it inside and out an hour ahead if you can.
Halve two oranges and a cinnamon stick into the cavity. Sit the bird on a bed of thickly sliced onion.
Roast 1 hour 10, basting twice with the pan juices. Rest it 15 minutes, uncovered.
While it rests, char radicchio or chicory in the chicken fat, 3 minutes, and dress with the resting juices.
Carve at the table. NON3 straight from the fridge, in a wine glass.
fields.why: Fatty skin needs tannin and this is the grippiest bottle in the range. Bitter greens meet the orange pith in the glass, so the plate and the pour finish on the same note.

fields.title: Miso-glazed eggplant, sesame, yuzu kosho
fields.intro: Vegetarian, and heavier than most meat. Every element is either caramelised or bitter, which is where NON3 lives.
steps: Halve three eggplants, score the flesh deeply, salt them and leave 20 minutes. Pat dry.
Fry cut-side down in a generous amount of oil until deep brown, 8 minutes. Turn and cook 5 more.
Whisk 3 tbsp white miso, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp water and a splash of NON3. Brush on thickly.
Grill hard for 4 minutes until the glaze blisters and catches at the edges.
Finish with toasted sesame, spring onion and a small spoon of yuzu kosho. Serve NON3 chilled.
fields.why: Eggplant has no fat of its own, so the pairing has to come from bitterness and salt. The yuzu on the plate is the yuzu in the bottle — that is not a coincidence, it is the same flavour logic.

fields.title: Green mango salad, chilli, peanuts
fields.intro: Sharp, salty, hot. The bottle is the only thing on the table that can cool it down.
steps: Julienne one green mango and half a cucumber. Keep them in cold water until you dress it.
Pound two red chillies, a clove of garlic and a teaspoon of salt into a rough paste.
Add lime juice, a teaspoon of sugar and fish sauce (or soy). Taste — it should be aggressive.
Drain the mango well, toss with the dressing, mint and coriander. Peanuts last so they stay crisp.
Serve NON5 as cold as you can get it.
fields.why: Alcohol amplifies capsaicin — this is the one clear advantage of 0.0%. NON5 carries 140mg of salt and hard verjus acid, both of which cool chilli instead of stoking it.

fields.title: Slow lamb shoulder, chickpeas, preserved lemon
fields.intro: Four hours of fat and spice, cut by the sharpest bottle in the range.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Rub the shoulder hard with salt, cumin, coriander seed and a little cinnamon.
Sear it in a heavy pot, then add a chopped onion, a tin of chickpeas with their liquid and 300ml water.
Cover and cook 3 hours, until a spoon goes through the meat with no resistance.
Lift the lid, raise to 200°C and roast 20 minutes to crisp the top.
Stir chopped preserved lemon and coriander through the chickpeas. NON5 very cold, in a wine glass.
ingredients: Cumin and coriander seed — 1 tbsp each
fields.why: Braise fat needs cutting, and the hop bitterness plus the bead here do the job a dry sparkling would. Preserved lemon on the plate lines up with the lemon verbena and myrtle in the glass.

fields.title: Whole fish in banana leaf, lemongrass, hibiscus
fields.intro: Steamed in its own leaf, opened at the table. Every aromatic in the parcel is also in the bottle.
steps: Blitz lemongrass, ginger, garlic, two chillies, a tablespoon of salt and the juice of two limes to a paste.
Score a whole snapper on both sides and pack the paste into the cuts and the cavity.
Wrap tightly in softened banana leaf. Grill over medium coals 18 minutes a side, or 200°C oven for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile reduce 100ml NON5 with dried hibiscus and a teaspoon of sugar to a sharp glaze.
Open the parcel at the table, spoon the hibiscus glaze over, and pour the rest very cold.
fields.why: Lemongrass, hibiscus and menthol are literally in this bottle, so the parcel smells like the glass when you open it. Reducing some of the NON5 into a glaze makes the link explicit rather than theoretical.
